rationale: Round-3 duty: verify the one-commit diff 0783a507..a8ac1fc4 (8 files, +199/-38) does not disturb my round-2 whole-branch fidelity basis (R1-R7 + R3.6/R6.7, the four OQ resolutions, the M/R/S/G/T protocol letter) and introduces no divergence from spec.md/plan.md. CONFIRMED. The only behavioral change is in internal/complete/complete.go: the metadata seam pair's production defaults move from bead.MergeMetadata/bead.GetMetadata to the named wrappers mergeMetadataEscaped/getMetadataEscaped, which route any returned error through next.RenderBDError. I checked the fidelity-relevant properties directly: (a) bdRenderedError preserves Unwrap (internal/next/beads.go:262), so errors.Is/As classification through the seam is unchanged — the new real-chain test asserts errors.As still reaches *exec.ExitError, and the lineage/sentinel classifications in complete.go are untouched; (b) the two sinks that ALREADY render through next.RenderBDError (materialize.go:160's attestation refusal and complete.go:1391's lock-failure DescribeLockFailure) now double-wrap — I verified renderBDError is idempotent on its own output (termsafe.Escape is identity on printable ASCII, and a strconv.Quote'd recovery line begins with a quote so it no longer matches guard.RecoveryPrefix), so no double-escaping or message drift; (c) the write-ahead attestation ordering (attest-before-publish, refuse-before-publish on failure, mismatch ⇒ FOREIGN clear + full normal run, read failure propagates) is byte-for-byte the round-2 design — no change to the discriminator, the S-stage staging, or any gate ordering, so the M/R/S/G/T protocol and OQ-1(a) are undisturbed; (d) the seam signature is identical, so phase.WithPhaseWriteLock's writer (complete.go:1381) and the R3.3 writer-inventory fence are unaffected (no new mindspec_phase writer). The pointer pin now pins the wrappers (named functions, not closures), so the family-wide escape cannot silently regress. Docs: the ADR-0041 'Honest trust boundary' paragraph and the materialize.go comments are honesty DISCLOSURES, not design changes — they state the resume optimization trusts the local operator environment's bd store and cite follow-up mindspec-an8q; this is consistent with R4's convergence contract (fail-closed direction preserved) and with my round-2 INFO on the bd coupling. The rewritten crash-window comment enumerates both windows correctly against the code (attest-then-CAS ordering; the C→D window demotes a legitimate marker to FOREIGN, degrading to the fully gated path — cost-a-resume, never admit-one). The lifecycle-modes.md 'two eights' sentence now matches agreement_table_test.go exactly: seven ordinary rows + terminal row hardcoded; forced-backward row seeds from the record but is held by the two setup guards at lines 851-854 (DerivePhaseFromChildren equality + IsBackwardMove). The bead-2 attribution for advancePhaseOnClaim is correct (cmd/mindspec/next.go:548 says Bead 2). The three line-number citations replaced by function anchors (repair.go, approve/plan.go ×2) are accurate. Empirical: go build ./... clean; go vet ./internal/complete clean; go test -short -count=1 on internal/complete (80.9s), internal/phase, internal/approve, internal/next all ok at a8ac1fc4 under my own GOCACHE; the new TestMetadataSeamEscapedDefaults_RealChainHostileStderr is hermetic (t.TempDir PATH shim, t.Setenv) and passes. Worktree left byte-identical (only the panel review dir is untracked).

findings.title: Two sinks now double-render through next.RenderBDError — verified idempotent, no action
findings.detail: materialize.go:160 and complete.go:1391 wrap an error that the escaped seam defaults have already wrapped. renderBDError(renderBDError(e)) == renderBDError(e): termsafe.Escape leaves printable ASCII untouched (so an already-quoted line is identity), and a quoted recovery line starts with '"' and no longer matches guard.RecoveryPrefix. Recorded so a future reader does not mistake the redundancy for a bug or 'fix' it by removing the outer wrap at a sink that could later take a non-seam error.

findings.title: Trust-boundary disclosure is fidelity-neutral
findings.detail: The ADR-0041 paragraph and materialize.go doc comments narrow the CLAIM (git-only forgery dead; bd-capable actor narrowed-not-closed; resume trusts the local operator environment) without changing any gate, ordering, or OQ resolution. Follow-up mindspec-an8q (signature-verified escalation) is cited; I did not verify the bead's existence (read-only review, no bd calls).
